findings.title: Learner exit no longer drains or stops the follower log processor (update-introduced)
findings.attribution: introduced by the update: PRIOR control Update-control-prior-leak-gap.cfg exhaustive (238,362 states) without violation; real old revision joins its SyncThread on learner exit, new revision leaks it (spec/output/harness/upd-serving-exit-v3.surefire-output.txt vs old-control output)
findings.summary: The update changed Learner.shutdown() to call zk.shutdown(boolean), which is not overridden by LearnerZooKeeperServer; the override shutdown() was the only code that shut down and drained the follower's SyncRequestProcessor. After a learner exit while serving, the old processor thread keeps running on the shared txn log (thread leak, observed in a real 3-node test: two live SyncThread per follower after one leader loss, leaked threads survive QuorumPeer shutdown), and txns queued at exit are written later, asynchronously. If a txn was already applied in memory but not yet flushed, the follower advertises it in the next sync, the leader DIFFs past it, and the follower's recoverable log misses a committed txn until the leaked thread writes it; a crash in that window, or a TRUNC that reopens the log before the stale append, leaves a committed gap or stale out-of-order records that restart replay applies.

findings.title: TRUNC-mode learner exit before NEWLEADER keeps an unpersisted in-memory image (pre-existing; not covered by the update)
findings.attribution: pre-existing: same violations under PRIOR (Update-control-prior-trunc.cfg, Update-control-prior-trunc-noleak-gap.cfg); the update fixes the SNAP branch only
findings.summary: SNAP and TRUNC both keep writeToTxnLog=false until NEWLEADER, apply in-sync COMMITs directly to the in-memory DataTree and persist them only via the NEWLEADER snapshot. The update forces a full shutdown (zkDb.clear) on learner exit only when syncMode is SNAP. A follower whose log is ahead of the leader's committed log (e.g. after a crash, while the leader has committed but not applied a txn) gets TRUNC followed by PROPOSAL+COMMIT for that txn, applies it only in memory, and if it fails before NEWLEADER it keeps the unpersisted image; it re-joins by DIFF from that zxid, logs later txns, and its recoverable log misses the committed txn, so after a restart it permanently lacks it.

findings.title: Fast-forward before drain leaves re-sent or stale records ahead of committed history in a follower log (pre-existing)
findings.attribution: pre-existing in the old revision (PRIOR); also reachable under UPDATED through the leaked processor (MC-1 variants)
findings.summary: On a learner exit while serving, the old LearnerZooKeeperServer.shutdown() fast-forwards the DataTree from the log before draining the sync queue, so queued txns are written to the log but are missing from the in-memory baseline advertised in the next sync. The leader re-sends them and the follower appends them again, so the log temporarily holds a record after a newer one (<<1,2,1>>) or an uncommitted record before a committed one. Restart replay applies every record in file order, so a crash in that window regresses state while lastProcessedZxid stays at the newer zxid.
